# The wanting-liking split

Wanting and liking come apart. The pull toward a thing and the pleasure of having it run on different machinery, so it is possible to want intensely something that brings little pleasure, and to enjoy something we never seek out.

## Notes

- Wanting is cue-driven: a notification, a smell, a shop window.
- Liking is quieter and does not grow with repetition in the same way.
- Habits and compulsions are wanting with the liking worn off.

This is the psychological cousin of the [[Hedonic treadmill]]: adaptation dulls liking while the cues keep the wanting sharp.
